stories.title: Schema: two venues as peers, divergence stored with its tolerance
Coinbase fetcher — fields by name, UTC alignment asserted per venue
Timestamp equality gates the comparison
Divergence computed and stored against the registry tolerance
A missing bar at the second venue is NOT_CORROBORATED, not an error
Single-source indicators are marked uncorroborated, visibly
Divergence reaches the page

results.note: compute_divergence_bps divides by the midpoint of the two values (ingest/corroborate.py:50-54), not by either source_a or source_b. The test at tests/test_divergence.py:81-88 asserts forward==reverse for swapped argument order and that the result differs from what dividing by either single value (100.0 or 101.0) would produce, directly proving the comparison is order-independent / not judged against either venue's value.

CorroborationDefinition.tolerance_bps is nested inside each IndicatorDefinition (registry.py:27-51), not a module-level constant. tests/test_divergence.py:91-130 loads a registry with two indicators carrying different tolerance_bps (25 vs 40) and shows the same 35bps divergence is DIVERGED under one and CORROBORATED under the other, proving tolerance is per-indicator rather than global.

record_corroboration (ingest/corroborate.py:100-122) inserts with 'on conflict (datapoint_a_id, datapoint_b_id) do nothing' and falls back to selecting the already-stored row rather than re-computing. The parametrized test directly asserts a defect-magnitude divergence (35.0 bps, above the 25 bps registry tolerance) is judged DIVERGED and a honest-disagreement-magnitude divergence (13.0 bps, below tolerance) is judged CORROBORATED — a direct assertion of the specific failure mode (a real defect crossing the threshold) the PRD exists to catch.

This pins approximations, not the measured values the criterion names, so the specific regression protection the criterion asks for is not actually in place.
